summary: Big-O notation describes how the number of steps an algorithm takes grows with the input size n. This program counts steps for O(n), O(log n), and O(n^2) code at three sizes.
notes: steps++ inside each loop counts work directly, so the table is the same on every computer.
When n grows 10 times, linearSearch grows 10 times, binarySearch grows by only about 3 steps, and countPairs grows 100 times.
Array.from({ length: n }, (_, i) => i) builds the sorted array 0, 1, ..., n - 1, like Python's list(range(n)).
pitfall: Using performance.now() to compare algorithms on small inputs gives different numbers on every run, and the first run is often slower while Node warms up. Count steps when you want a fair comparison.
contrast: Steps are counted the same way in all three languages. To time code, JavaScript uses performance.now(), which returns milliseconds as a decimal, where Python uses time.perf_counter() and Java uses System.nanoTime().
